Kyou shukudai aru.forms: aru (u-verb) → aru: unchanged plain nonpast, “have / exist.”
Kyou shukudai aru.particles: Shukudai is what exists; ga is omitted in this casual question. No ka is needed with rising intonation.
Kyou shukudai aru.past: Change aru → atta: Kinou shukudai atta? = Did you have homework yesterday?
Kyou shukudai aru.swap: Replace shukudai with jikan: Jikan aru? = Do you have time?

Uun shukudai nai.forms: aru → nai: irregular plain negative, “do not have.”
Uun shukudai nai.particles: Uun means no. Shukudai is what you do not have; casual speech omits ga.
Uun shukudai nai.past: nai → nakatta: Uun, shukudai nakatta. = No, I did not have homework.
Uun shukudai nai.swap: Swap shukudai for jikan: Uun, jikan nai. = No, I do not have time.

Nihonjin.forms: Nihonjin is a noun, not a verb. Omit da in a casual noun question.
Nihonjin.particles: No particle is needed here; the listener and topic are understood.
Nihonjin.past: Nihonjin datta? = Were you Japanese? Grammatically possible, but an unusual question unless nationality changed. Gakusei datta? (Were you a student?) is a more natural past example.
Nihonjin.swap: Nihonjin → daigakusei: Daigakusei? = Are you a college student?

Uun Nihonjin janai.forms: Noun + janai is the plain negative of noun + da.
Uun Nihonjin janai.particles: Uun answers no; the subject is understood.
Uun Nihonjin janai.past: janai → janakatta: Uun, Nihonjin janakatta. = No, [the person] was not Japanese.
Uun Nihonjin janai.swap: Nihonjin → gakusei: Uun, gakusei janai. = No, I am not a student.

Mainichi nihongo o hanasu.forms: hanasu (u-verb) is the plain nonpast of hanashimasu.
Mainichi nihongo o hanasu.particles: O marks nihongo as the language spoken. Mainichi usually takes no ni.
Mainichi nihongo o hanasu.past: hanasu → hanashita: Kinou nihongo o hanashita? = Did you speak Japanese yesterday?
Mainichi nihongo o hanasu.swap: Nihongo → eigo: Mainichi eigo o hanasu? = Do you speak English every day?

Uun mainichi nihongo o hanasanai.particles: O marks the language. Mainichi + negative means not every day, not necessarily never.
Uun mainichi nihongo o hanasanai.past: hanasanai → hanasanakatta: Kinou nihongo o hanasanakatta. = I did not speak Japanese yesterday.
Uun mainichi nihongo o hanasanai.swap: Nihongo → eigo; retain o before the verb.

Atsui.forms: Atsui is an i-adjective, not a verb; it can end a plain sentence by itself.
Atsui.particles: No particles are needed in this short question about the weather.
Atsui.past: atsui → atsukatta: Kinou atsukatta? = Was it hot yesterday?
Atsui.swap: Atsui → samui: Samui? = Is it cold?

Uun atsukunai.forms: atsui → atsukunai: remove the final i and add kunai.
Uun atsukunai.particles: Uun is the informal no; the weather topic is understood.
Uun atsukunai.past: atsukunai → atsukunakatta: Uun, atsukunakatta. = No, it was not hot.
Uun atsukunai.swap: Samui → samukunai: Uun, samukunai. = No, it is not cold.

Yamashita sensei wa kakkoii to omoimasu.forms: omou (u-verb) → omoimasu. Kakkoii is an i-adjective; no da before to.
Yamashita sensei wa kakkoii to omoimasu.particles: Wa marks Professor Yamashita as the topic. To introduces the thought: “is good-looking.”
Yamashita sensei wa kakkoii to omoimasu.past: omoimasu → omoimashita = I thought he was good-looking. Kakkoii → kakkoyokatta before to omoimasu = I think he was good-looking. These shift different parts of the sentence.
Yamashita sensei wa kakkoii to omoimasu.swap: Yamashita sensei → Tanaka-san; or kakkoii → yasashii (kind).

Kono machi wa omoshirokunai to omoimasu.forms: omoshiroi → omoshirokunai; omou → omoimasu. Literally “I think [this town is not interesting].”
Kono machi wa omoshirokunai to omoimasu.particles: Wa marks the town; to quotes the entire negative description.
Kono machi wa omoshirokunai to omoimasu.past: Omoshirokunakatta to omoimasu = I think it was not interesting. Omoshirokunai to omoimashita = I thought it was not interesting.
Kono machi wa omoshirokunai to omoimasu.swap: Kono machi → kono eiga: Kono eiga wa omoshirokunai to omoimasu. = I do not think this movie is interesting.

Mado o akenaide kudasai.forms: akeru (ru-verb) → akenai → akenaide kudasai: please do not open.
Mado o akenaide kudasai.particles: O marks mado as the object. De here belongs to the negative request ending, not a location particle.
Mado o akenaide kudasai.past: A request itself does not become past tense. To report a past action: Mado o akemasen deshita (polite) / Mado o akenakatta (plain) = I did not open the window.
Mado o akenaide kudasai.swap: Mado → doa: Doa o akenaide kudasai. = Please do not open the door.

Kasa o wasurenaide kudasai.particles: O marks the thing that must not be forgotten.
Kasa o wasurenaide kudasai.past: For a past statement: Kasa o wasuremasen deshita / Kasa o wasurenakatta = I did not forget my umbrella. Do not conjugate kudasai as a past request.
Kasa o wasurenaide kudasai.swap: Kasa → shukudai: Shukudai o wasurenaide kudasai. = Please do not forget your homework.

Tanaka-san wa daigakusei janai to iimash.forms: iu (u-verb) → iimasu → iimashita. Daigakusei janai is a negative noun predicate.
Tanaka-san wa daigakusei janai to iimash.particles: Wa marks the speaker; to marks the reported words.
Tanaka-san wa daigakusei janai to iimash.past: Iimashita is already past (“said”). Daigakusei janakatta to iimashita = he said he had not been / was not a college student at the relevant earlier time. Japanese does not automatically shift every quoted verb into past tense.

Tanaka-san wa kekkon shite inai to iimas.forms: kekkon suru → kekkon shite iru → kekkon shite inai. Iu → iimashita.
Tanaka-san wa kekkon shite inai to iimas.particles: Wa marks Tanaka as speaker; to encloses the reported state.
Tanaka-san wa kekkon shite inai to iimas.past: Iimashita is already past. Shite inai → shite inakatta changes the reported state to “was not married.”
Tanaka-san wa kekkon shite inai to iimas.swap: Tanaka-san → ani: Ani wa kekkon shite inai to iimashita. = My older brother said he is not married.

Mearii-san wa mainichi tanoshii to iimas.forms: Tanoshii is an i-adjective; iu → iimashita. No da after tanoshii.
Mearii-san wa mainichi tanoshii to iimas.particles: Wa marks Mary; to quotes mainichi tanoshii, “every day is fun.”
Mearii-san wa mainichi tanoshii to iimas.past: Iimashita is already past. Tanoshii → tanoshikatta makes the quoted description past: every day was fun.
Mearii-san wa mainichi tanoshii to iimas.swap: Mainichi → ryokou: Mearii-san wa ryokou ga tanoshikatta to iimashita. = Mary said the trip was fun.

Mearii-san wa amari sake o nomanai to ii.particles: O marks sake; amari + negative means not much; to marks the quote.
Mearii-san wa amari sake o nomanai to ii.past: Iimashita is already past. Nomanai → nomanakatta changes the quote to “did not drink much.”
Mearii-san wa amari sake o nomanai to ii.swap: Sake → koohii: Mearii-san wa amari koohii o nomanai to iimashita.

Mearii-san wa mikan ga suki da to iimash.forms: Suki is a na-adjective: suki da before to. Iu → iimashita.
Mearii-san wa mikan ga suki da to iimash.particles: Ga marks what Mary likes; to quotes the statement; wa marks Mary.
Mearii-san wa mikan ga suki da to iimash.past: Iimashita is already past. Suki da → suki datta changes the quote to “liked.”
Mearii-san wa mikan ga suki da to iimash.swap: Mikan → ringo: Mearii-san wa ringo ga suki da to iimashita. = Mary said she likes apples.

Watashi wa e o kaku no ga jouzu desu.forms: kaku (u-verb) stays in dictionary form before no. Jouzu is a na-adjective.
Watashi wa e o kaku no ga jouzu desu.particles: O marks pictures as the object; no turns e o kaku into “drawing”; ga marks the activity you are good at; wa marks you as topic.
Watashi wa e o kaku no ga jouzu desu.past: Jouzu desu → jouzu deshita = I was good at drawing. Keep kaku in dictionary form: kaita no would refer to a past drawing event.
Watashi wa e o kaku no ga jouzu desu.swap: E o kaku → uta o utau: Watashi wa uta o utau no ga jouzu desu. = I am good at singing.

Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga jouzu j.forms: suru is irregular but unchanged before no. Jouzu janai desu means not good at.
Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga jouzu j.particles: O marks sports; no makes “doing sports” a noun phrase; ga marks the skill being evaluated.
Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga jouzu j.past: Jouzu janai desu → jouzu janakatta desu = I was not good at sports. Suru remains nonpast because the activity is general.
Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga jouzu j.swap: Supootsu o suru → oyogu: Watashi wa oyogu no ga jouzu janai desu. = I am not good at swimming.

Watashi wa jimu ni iku no ga suki desu.forms: iku stays in dictionary form before no; suki is a na-adjective.
Watashi wa jimu ni iku no ga suki desu.particles: Ni marks gym as destination; no makes “going to the gym” an activity; ga marks what you like.
Watashi wa jimu ni iku no ga suki desu.past: Suki desu → suki deshita = I liked going to the gym. Keep iku unchanged.
Watashi wa jimu ni iku no ga suki desu.swap: Jimu → toshokan: Watashi wa toshokan ni iku no ga suki desu. = I like going to the library.

Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga kir.forms: unten suru is a suru-verb; no follows its dictionary form. Kirai is a na-adjective despite ending in i.
Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga kir.particles: O marks the car; no turns driving into a noun phrase; ga marks what you dislike.
Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga kir.past: Kirai desu → kirai deshita = I disliked driving. Do not use kiraikatta.
Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga kir.swap: Kuruma o unten suru → souji suru: Watashi wa souji suru no ga kirai desu. = I dislike cleaning.

Konnichiwa. Ogenki desu ka?.forms: Konnichiwa is a greeting; genki is a na-adjective. Desu makes the question polite.
Konnichiwa. Ogenki desu ka?.particles: O- is a polite prefix in ogenki; ka marks the question.
Konnichiwa. Ogenki desu ka?.past: Ogenki deshita ka? = Were you well? Konnichiwa has no tense.
Konnichiwa. Ogenki desu ka?.swap: Ogenki desu ka? → Oisogashii desu ka? = Are you busy? (Different adjective type; do not copy na-adjective rules onto isogashii.)

Toukyou no tenki wa dou desu ka?.forms: Dou desu ka asks how something is. There is no action verb here.
Toukyou no tenki wa dou desu ka?.particles: No links Tokyo and its weather; wa marks the weather as topic; ka makes the question.
Toukyou no tenki wa dou desu ka?.past: Toukyou no tenki wa dou deshita ka? = How was the weather in Tokyo?
Toukyou no tenki wa dou desu ka?.swap: Toukyou → Oosaka: Oosaka no tenki wa dou desu ka?

San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yoi desu..forms: Yoi is the standard form related to ii (good), an i-adjective.
San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yoi desu..particles: No links the city and weather; wa marks the topic.
San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yoi desu..past: Yoi → yokatta: San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yokatta desu. = The weather was nice. Desu stays desu with a past i-adjective.
San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yoi desu..swap: Yoi → samui: San Furanshisuko no tenki wa samui desu. = The weather is cold.

Watashi ni wa chichi to haha to imouto g.forms: iru (ru-verb) → imasu: people exist / I have family members. Hitori means one person.
Watashi ni wa chichi to haha to imouto g.particles: Ni wa presents your situation; to lists family; ga marks who exists. Hitori is intended to count the younger sister here.
Watashi ni wa chichi to haha to imouto g.past: Imasu → imashita = I had / there were these family members. A past form can suggest a changed family situation, so use it only when intended.
Watashi ni wa chichi to haha to imouto g.swap: Imouto ga hitori → imouto ga futari (two younger sisters). A clearer standalone count is Watashi ni wa imouto ga hitori imasu.

Chichi to haha wa Ookurando ni sunde ima.forms: sumu (u-verb) → sunde + iru → sunde imasu: live / reside.
Chichi to haha wa Ookurando ni sunde ima.particles: To joins father and mother; wa marks them as topic; ni marks residence.
Chichi to haha wa Ookurando ni sunde ima.past: Sunde imasu → sunde imashita = lived / were living. The auxiliary iru changes tense; sunde stays the same.
Chichi to haha wa Ookurando ni sunde ima.swap: Ookurando → Toukyou: Chichi to haha wa Toukyou ni sunde imasu.

Demo, imouto wa San Diego ni sunde imasu.forms: sumu → sunde imasu. Demo introduces a contrast.
Demo, imouto wa San Diego ni sunde imasu.particles: Wa marks the younger sister; ni marks where she lives.
Demo, imouto wa San Diego ni sunde imasu.past: Sunde imasu → sunde imashita = my younger sister lived there.
Demo, imouto wa San Diego ni sunde imasu.swap: Imouto → ani: Demo, ani wa San Diego ni sunde imasu. = But my older brother lives in San Diego.

Chichi wa rokujussai desu..forms: Rokujussai is an age expression, not a verb. Desu is the polite copula.
Chichi wa rokujussai desu..particles: Wa marks father as the topic.
Chichi wa rokujussai desu..past: Desu → deshita: Chichi wa rokujussai deshita. = My father was 60.
Chichi wa rokujussai desu..swap: Rokujussai → gojussai: Chichi wa gojussai desu. = My father is 50.

Haha wa gojussai desu..forms: Gojussai is an age expression; desu is the polite ending.
Haha wa gojussai desu..particles: Wa marks mother as the topic.
Haha wa gojussai desu..past: Haha wa gojussai deshita. = My mother was 50.
Haha wa gojussai desu..swap: Gojussai → rokujussai: Haha wa rokujussai desu. = My mother is 60.

Imouto wa juuhassai desu..forms: Juuhassai means eighteen years old; desu links it to the topic.
Imouto wa juuhassai desu..past: Imouto wa juuhassai deshita. = My younger sister was 18.
Imouto wa juuhassai desu..swap: Juuhassai → juukyuusai: Imouto wa juukyuusai desu. = My younger sister is 19.

Chichi wa kensetsu no shigoto o shite im.forms: suru → shite + iru → shite imasu: doing work / working in an occupation.
Chichi wa kensetsu no shigoto o shite im.particles: Wa marks father; no describes the kind of work; o marks shigoto as the object of suru.
Chichi wa kensetsu no shigoto o shite im.past: Shite imasu → shite imashita = worked / was working. Change the final auxiliary, not shite.
Chichi wa kensetsu no shigoto o shite im.swap: Kensetsu → jimu: Chichi wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu. = My father does office work.

Haha wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu..forms: suru → shite imasu. Jimu here means office administration, not the gym (jimu in katakana).
Haha wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu..particles: Wa marks mother; no connects office work to shigoto; o marks the object.
Haha wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu..past: Shite imasu → shite imashita = my mother did office work.
Haha wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu..swap: Haha → ani: Ani wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu.

Imouto wa daigakusei desu..forms: Daigakusei is a noun. Desu is the polite copula; plain form is da.
Imouto wa daigakusei desu..particles: Wa marks the younger sister as topic.
Imouto wa daigakusei desu..past: Desu → deshita: Imouto wa daigakusei deshita. = My younger sister was a college student.
Imouto wa daigakusei desu..swap: Daigakusei → kaishain: Imouto wa kaishain desu. = My younger sister is a company employee.

Chichi to terebi o mimasu..forms: miru (ru-verb) → mimasu: drop ru and add masu.
Chichi to terebi o mimasu..particles: To means with father; o marks TV as what you watch. The subject I is understood.
Chichi to terebi o mimasu..past: Mimasu → mimashita (polite); miru → mita (plain). Chichi to terebi o mimashita. = I watched TV with my father.
Chichi to terebi o mimasu..swap: Terebi → eiga: Chichi to eiga o mimasu. = I watch a movie with my father.

Haha to haikingu ni ikimasu..forms: iku (u-verb) → ikimasu. Haikingu ni iku is go hiking.
Haha to haikingu ni ikimasu..particles: To marks mother as companion; ni marks the activity you go to do.
Haha to haikingu ni ikimasu..past: Ikimasu → ikimashita (polite); iku → itta (irregular plain past).
Haha to haikingu ni ikimasu..swap: Haha → tomodachi: Tomodachi to haikingu ni ikimasu. = I go hiking with friends.

Imouto to geemu o shimasu..particles: The first to follows imouto (with my sister); o marks games as the object.
Imouto to geemu o shimasu..swap: Geemu → tenisu: Imouto to tenisu o shimasu. = I play tennis with my younger sister.

Sore dewa, minasan ni oai suru no o tano.forms: au → oai suru is a humble expression for meeting. Suru stays nonpast before no; shite imasu comes from suru + iru.
Sore dewa, minasan ni oai suru no o tano.particles: Ni marks whom you meet; no turns meeting into a noun phrase; o marks what you look forward to; ni belongs to tanoshimi ni suru.
Sore dewa, minasan ni oai suru no o tano.past: Final shite imasu → shite imashita = I was looking forward to meeting you all. Keep oai suru unchanged because the meeting was still anticipated at that time.
Sore dewa, minasan ni oai suru no o tano.swap: Minasan → sensei: Sensei ni oai suru no o tanoshimi ni shite imasu. = I look forward to meeting the teacher.

Yoroshiku onegai shimasu..forms: Onegai suru → onegai shimasu: a set polite request / closing, not a literal universal “thank you.”
Yoroshiku onegai shimasu..particles: No standalone particles occur in this expression. Yoroshiku modifies the request.
Yoroshiku onegai shimasu..past: Do not mechanically turn this greeting into a past-tense closing. Onegai shimashita means “I asked / requested,” a different statement.
Yoroshiku onegai shimasu..swap: For a more formal closing: Yoroshiku onegai itashimasu. Keep the set phrase intact.

Arekkusu yori.forms: A signature fragment, not a verb sentence; there is no dictionary verb to conjugate.
Arekkusu yori.particles: Yori means from and follows the sender’s name.
Arekkusu yori.past: No tense change: a name + yori signature is the same in a letter about past or present events.
Arekkusu yori.swap: Arekkusu → Mearii: Mearii yori = From Mary.

Watashi wa taitei asa hachiji goro okiru.forms: okiru (ru-verb) stays plain nonpast to describe a routine.
Watashi wa taitei asa hachiji goro okiru.particles: Wa marks the speaker; goro means around and follows the time.
Watashi wa taitei asa hachiji goro okiru.swap: Hachiji → shichiji: Asa shichiji goro okiru. = I wake around 7 a.m.

Sorekara, tsumetai shawaa o abite, asago.forms: abiru → abite; taberu → tabete (ru-verbs). Iku ends the sequence.
Sorekara, tsumetai shawaa o abite, asago.particles: O marks shower and breakfast; de marks transport; ni marks destination.
Sorekara, tsumetai shawaa o abite, asago.past: Change final iku → itta: abite and tabete stay in te-form. The whole sequence is then past.
Sorekara, tsumetai shawaa o abite, asago.swap: Basu de → densha de (by train); shigoto ni → gakkou ni (to school).

Gogo wa konpyuutaa de muzukashii mondai.forms: toku (u-verb) means solve; not to talk.
Gogo wa konpyuutaa de muzukashii mondai.particles: Wa marks afternoon as topic; de marks the computer as tool; o marks problems.
Gogo wa konpyuutaa de muzukashii mondai.swap: Muzukashii → yasashii (easy): yasashii mondai o toku = solve easy problems.

Shigoto wa isogashikute taihen da..forms: isogashii → isogashikute joins descriptions; taihen is a na-adjective.
Shigoto wa isogashikute taihen da..past: Change final da → datta: Shigoto wa isogashikute taihen datta. = Work was busy and tough.
Shigoto wa isogashikute taihen da..swap: Shigoto → gakkou: Gakkou wa isogashikute taihen da. = School is busy and tough.

Sorekara, tomodachi to koohii o nomi ni.forms: nomu → nomimasu → nomi (stem); iku → itte; kyuukei suru = take a break.
Sorekara, tomodachi to koohii o nomi ni.particles: To marks friends as companions; o marks coffee; stem + ni gives the purpose of going.
Sorekara, tomodachi to koohii o nomi ni.past: Change final suru → shita; itte remains te-form.
Sorekara, tomodachi to koohii o nomi ni.swap: Koohii → ocha: ocha o nomi ni iku = go to drink tea.

Koohii wa tsumetakute oishii..forms: tsumetai → tsumetakute joins descriptions; oishii stays nonpast.
Koohii wa tsumetakute oishii..past: Oishii → oishikatta: Koohii wa tsumetakute oishikatta. = The coffee was cold and delicious.
Koohii wa tsumetakute oishii..swap: Tsumetakute → atatakakute: Koohii wa atatakakute oishii. = The coffee is warm and delicious.

Gogo goji made ni ie ni kaeru..forms: kaeru (u-verb) means return; do not treat it as a ru-verb.
Gogo goji made ni ie ni kaeru..particles: Made ni marks the deadline; ie ni marks home as destination.
Gogo goji made ni ie ni kaeru..swap: Goji → rokuji: Gogo rokuji made ni ie ni kaeru. = I return home by 6 p.m.

Soshite, atatakai bangohan o tabete, tom.forms: taberu → tabete; suru ends the linked sequence.
Soshite, atatakai bangohan o tabete, tom.particles: O marks dinner and games; to marks friends as companions.
Soshite, atatakai bangohan o tabete, tom.past: Change final suru → shita; tabete remains te-form.
Soshite, atatakai bangohan o tabete, tom.swap: Tomodachi to → imouto to: play with your younger sister instead.

Demo, watashitachi wa geemu ga amari jou.forms: jouzu is a na-adjective; janai is its plain negative.
Demo, watashitachi wa geemu ga amari jou.particles: Wa marks we; ga marks games as the skill; amari plus negative means not very.
Demo, watashitachi wa geemu ga amari jou.past: Janai → janakatta: Geemu ga amari jouzu janakatta. = We were not very good at games.
Demo, watashitachi wa geemu ga amari jou.swap: Geemu → tenisu: Watashitachi wa tenisu ga amari jouzu janai.

Shuumatsu wa jimu ni iku..forms: iku is plain nonpast, describing a weekend habit.
Shuumatsu wa jimu ni iku..particles: Wa marks weekends as time topic; ni marks gym as destination.
Shuumatsu wa jimu ni iku..past: Iku → itta: Shuumatsu wa jimu ni itta. = I went to the gym on the weekend.
Shuumatsu wa jimu ni iku..swap: Jimu → toshokan: Shuumatsu wa toshokan ni iku. = I go to the library on weekends.

Sorekara, tomodachi to asobu..forms: asobu (u-verb) means play / spend leisure time.
Sorekara, tomodachi to asobu..swap: Tomodachi → imouto: Sorekara, imouto to asobu. = Then I hang out with my younger sister.

Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga suk.forms: Unten suru means drive. Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Suki is a na-adjective, not a verb.
Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga suk.particles: Wa marks you as topic; o marks the car; no turns driving into an activity noun; ga marks what you like.
Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga suk.past: Suki desu → suki deshita = I liked driving. Keep unten suru unchanged for the general activity.
Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga suk.swap: Kuruma o unten suru → hon o yomu: Watashi wa hon o yomu no ga suki desu. = I like reading books.

Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimasu.forms: Unten suru → unten shimasu: polite nonpast. Itsumo means always.
Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimasu.particles: Wa marks you as topic; o marks the car being driven.
Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimasu.past: Shimasu → shimashita: Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimashita. = I always drove (in the period being discussed).
Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimasu.swap: Itsumo → tokidoki: Watashi wa tokidoki kuruma o unten shimasu. = I sometimes drive.

Unten wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoima.forms: Tanoshii → tanoshikute links two descriptions. Omou → omoimasu means think (polite).
Unten wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoima.particles: Wa marks driving; to marks the thought: fun and interesting.
Unten wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoima.past: Omoimasu → omoimashita = I thought driving was fun and interesting. To describe driving itself as past while keeping “I think,” use tanoshikute omoshirokatta to omoimasu.
Unten wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoima.swap: Unten → ryouri: Ryouri wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoimasu. = I think cooking is fun and interesting.

Watashi wa shashin o toru no ga kirai de.forms: Toru (u-verb) means take a photo; it stays in dictionary form before no. Kirai is a na-adjective. Muzukashii is an i-adjective.
Watashi wa shashin o toru no ga kirai de.particles: O marks photos; no turns taking photos into an activity; ga marks what you dislike; kara explains the reason.
Watashi wa shashin o toru no ga kirai de.past: Kirai desu → kirai deshita; muzukashii → muzukashikatta: I disliked taking photos because it was difficult. Keep toru nonpast for the general activity.
Watashi wa shashin o toru no ga kirai de.swap: Shashin o toru → oyogu: Watashi wa oyogu no ga kirai desu. Muzukashii kara desu. = I dislike swimming because it is difficult.

Sorekara, watashi wa ryouri o suru no ga.forms: Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Jouzu is a na-adjective. Omou stays plain before kara, even though the sentence ends politely.
Sorekara, watashi wa ryouri o suru no ga.particles: O marks cooking; no makes the activity a noun phrase; ga marks the skill; to marks the thought; kara means because.
Sorekara, watashi wa ryouri o suru no ga.past: Jouzu desu → jouzu deshita; omou → omotta: Omoshiroi to omotta kara desu = because I thought it was interesting. Do not automatically make every embedded word past.
Sorekara, watashi wa ryouri o suru no ga.swap: Ryouri o suru → e o kaku: Watashi wa e o kaku no ga jouzu desu. = I am good at drawing. Use this as a pattern; praising your own skill with jouzu can sound boastful in conversation.

Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga heta de.forms: Suru stays unchanged before no. Renshuu suru → renshuu shinai is the plain negative of practice. Heta is a na-adjective.
Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga heta de.particles: O marks sports; no makes doing sports an activity; ga marks the skill. Amari pairs with a negative for not much; kara gives the reason.
Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga heta de.past: Heta desu → heta deshita; shinai → shinakatta: Amari renshuu shinakatta kara desu = because I did not practice much.
Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga heta de.swap: Supootsu o suru → uta o utau: Watashi wa uta o utau no ga heta desu. = I am bad at singing.

Motto renshuu shimasu..forms: Renshuu suru → renshuu shimasu. Polite nonpast can express future intention; motto means more.
Motto renshuu shimasu..particles: No explicit particle is needed in this suru-verb phrase. The subject I is understood.
Motto renshuu shimasu..past: Shimasu → shimashita: Motto renshuu shimashita. = I practiced more.
Motto renshuu shimasu..swap: Renshuu → benkyou: Motto benkyou shimasu. = I will study more.

Kuroi shatsu o kite imasu..forms: Kiru (ru-verb, to put on upper-body clothing) → kite + imasu. The resulting state is “am wearing.” Kuroi is an i-adjective.
Kuroi shatsu o kite imasu..particles: O marks the shirt being worn. The subject I is understood.
Kuroi shatsu o kite imasu..past: Kite imasu → kite imashita = I was wearing a black shirt. Keep kite unchanged.
Kuroi shatsu o kite imasu..swap: Kuroi → shiroi: Shiroi shatsu o kite imasu. = I am wearing a white shirt.

Kuroi zubon o haite imasu..forms: Haku (u-verb, to put on lower-body clothing or footwear) → haite + imasu = am wearing. Ku → ite makes the te-form.
Kuroi zubon o haite imasu..particles: O marks the pants. Kuroi directly describes zubon; no na is needed.
Kuroi zubon o haite imasu..past: Haite imasu → haite imashita = I was wearing black pants.
Kuroi zubon o haite imasu..swap: Kuroi → aoi: Aoi zubon o haite imasu. = I am wearing blue pants.

Shiroi kutsu o haite imasu..forms: Haku → haite imasu is used for shoes as well as pants. Shiroi means white and is an i-adjective.
Shiroi kutsu o haite imasu..particles: O marks shoes as the item worn. The subject I is understood.
Shiroi kutsu o haite imasu..past: Haite imasu → haite imashita = I was wearing white shoes.
Shiroi kutsu o haite imasu..swap: Shiroi → kuroi: Kuroi kutsu o haite imasu. = I am wearing black shoes.

Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takai desu..forms: Mijikai → mijikakute links “hair is short” to the next description. Se ga takai literally means height is high. Both are i-adjectives.
Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takai desu..particles: The first ga marks hair as the subject of short; the second ga marks height as the subject of high. My is understood from context.
Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takai desu..past: Change final takai → takakatta: Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takakatta desu. = My hair was short and I was tall. Desu stays desu after the past i-adjective.
Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takai desu..swap: Mijikakute → nagakute: Kami ga nagakute, se ga takai desu. = My hair is long and I am tall.

Massugu itte,.forms: Iku (to go) → itte, the irregular te-form. Here it links “go straight” to the following instruction; it is not past tense.
Massugu itte,.particles: Massugu describes how to go. No particle is needed between this adverb and itte.
Massugu itte,.past: For a past statement, iku → itta: Massugu itta. = I went straight. The original is an instruction, not a past event.
Massugu itte,.swap: Replace massugu with yukkuri: Yukkuri itte. = Go slowly. This card is the opening segment of the full answer.

Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte ku.forms: Magaru (u-verb, to turn) → magatte + kudasai = please turn. Futatsume means second.
Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte ku.particles: No links second and corner. O marks the corner where you turn; ni marks the direction, left.
Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte ku.past: A request does not become a past request. To report the action: Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatta. = I turned left at the second corner.
Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte ku.swap: Hidari → migi: Futatsume no kado o migi ni magatte kudasai. = Turn right at the second corner. Futatsume → hitotsume changes it to the first corner.

Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu.forms: Aru (u-verb, to exist) → arimasu, polite nonpast. Use aru for a place or inanimate thing, not iru.
Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu.particles: Wa marks bookstore as topic; no links street to its left side; ni marks where it is; yo adds information for the listener.
Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu.past: Arimasu → arimashita: Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimashita. = The bookstore was on the left side of the street.
Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu.swap: Honya → ginkou and hidarigawa → migigawa: Ginkou wa michi no migigawa ni arimasu yo. = The bank is on the right side of the street.

Massugu itte, futatsume no kado o hidari.forms: Iku → itte connects the first instruction; magaru → magatte kudasai makes a polite request; aru → arimasu describes the bookstore location.
Massugu itte, futatsume no kado o hidari.particles: No links second to corner and street to left side. O marks the turning point; ni marks the turning direction and bookstore location. Wa marks the bookstore as topic; yo provides information.
Massugu itte, futatsume no kado o hidari.past: Instructions are requests, not past statements. To report the trip: Massugu itte, futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatta. Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimashita. = I went straight and turned left; the bookstore was on the left.
Massugu itte, futatsume no kado o hidari.swap: For a bank on the right, swap honya → ginkou, hidari → migi, and hidarigawa → migigawa. Keep the particles and sentence pattern.
